waypoints.name: Washington Pass

sections.advice: Sedro Woolley → Diablo Lake is 106 km of getting across. Ride it tidily and keep the enthusiasm for what comes after.
Diablo Lake → Washington Pass climbs about 1669 m in 51 km. This is the part worth slowing down for - look through the bends and use the pull-offs.
Washington Pass → Winthrop drops about 1669 m over 43 km. Brakes and eyes forward; the views are behind the corners, not in them.

north-cascades-scenic-highway.provenance: CURATED FROM THE ARCHIVE: waypoints taken from the named road North Cascades Scenic Highway. Distances between stops are great-circle with a road factor, not a routed measurement - the pipeline replaces them when it routes this line.

scenicChapters.title: Diablo Lake → Washington Pass
scenicChapters.narrative: The ground tilts up and stays tilted for 91 km. 1669 m of it, taken steadily rather than in one wall — a steady rhythm suits this better than bursts. The height arrives whether you hurry or not.

scenicChapters.title: Washington Pass → Winthrop
scenicChapters.narrative: 77 km that neither climbs nor drops much. The road settles into the ground rather than fighting it. This is where a day makes up time without anyone trying. Third and fourth, and very little else.

north-cascades-scenic-highway.story: 356 km from Sedro-Woolley to the finish, about 4 h 49 of riding. On the way it passes Diablo Lake and Washington Pass. The highest point is about 1,650 m. Washington Pass is subject to seasonal closure - check it is open before you set off. A steady touring day rather than a sprint.
